etymologies.etymologyHTML: From micro- +‎ wave.

definitions.definition: An electromagnetic wave with wavelength between that of infrared light and radio waves.

quote.citation: 1964 August, “The NER's microwave radio-telephone begins work”, in Modern Railways, page 129:
quote.text: Microwaves do not follow the curvature of the earth, but travel in a straight line. They must therefore have unobstructed "line of sight" and the dish aerials have to be sited on towers or high buildings, on high ground, or a combination of all three.

definitions.definition: (transitive) To cook (something) in a microwave oven.

quote.citation: 2011 December 14, Steven Morris, “Devon woman jailed for 168 days for killing kitten in microwave”, in Guardian‎[1]:
quote.text: A vengeful mother-of-three has been jailed for 168 days after being convicted of killing a neighbour's kitten by microwaving the 10-week-old pet.

definitions.definition: (transitive, slang) To provide minimal preparation for implementation, deeming full or extensive preparation as unnecessary.
